articleTitle: Integrating Big Data Governance and Corporate Strategies in Small and Medium Caspian Basin Seaports
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: This study investigates how stakeholders can integrate Big Data governance with corporate strategies in small and medium seaports in the Caspian Basin. The research uses a qualitative approach featuring semi-structured interviews with port executives, regulatory authority experts, and strategists. The data analysis reveals essential elements for successful integration, including stakeholder involvement, continuous training, effective communication, and collaboration. Based on the findings, the Structured Data Alignment Framework (SDAF) is developed, providing a six-step guideline: understanding corporate strategy, establishing a governance framework, integrating Big Data strategy, fostering communication and collaboration, building capacity through training, and ensuring continuous improvement. The study highlights that strategic alignment and robust data governance practices enhance operational efficiency, competitiveness, and sustainability, contributing to regional economic growth and environmental sustainability. Future research should focus on refining these themes and exploring the long-term impacts of Big Data integration in the maritime sector. The SDAF offers practical guidance for seaport managers and stakeholders, ensuring that digitalization efforts align with strategic objectives and drive positive social change.

articleTitle: Tiny Machine Learning for Real-Time Aquaculture Monitoring: A Case Study in Morocco
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: Aquaculture, the farming of aquatic organisms, is a rapidly growing industry facing challenges such as water quality fluctuations, disease outbreaks, and inefficient feed management. Traditional monitoring methods often rely on manual labor and are time consuming, leading to potential delays in addressing issues. This paper proposes the integration of low-power edge devices using Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) into aquaculture systems to enable real-time automated monitoring and control, such as collecting data and triggering alarms, and reducing labor requirements. The system provides real-time data on the required parameters such as pH levels, temperature, dissolved oxygen, and ammonia levels to control water quality, nutrient levels, and environmental conditions enabling better maintenance, efficient resource utilization, and optimal management of the enclosed aquaculture space. The system enables alerts in case of anomaly detection. The data collected by the sensors over time can serve for important decision-making regarding optimizing water treatment processes, feed distribution, feed pattern analysis and improve feed efficiency, reducing operational costs. This research explores the feasibility of developing TinyML-based solutions for aquaculture monitoring, considering factors such as sensor selection, algorithm design, hardware constraints, and ethical considerations. By demonstrating the potential benefits of TinyML in aquaculture, our aim is to contribute to the development of more sustainable and efficient farming practices.

articleTitle: The Impact of Redundancy on Resource Utilization in Vehicular Clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: Cloud computing has grown in its application and prevalence through the years, providing resources that would have otherwise limited use. Building upon the success of conventional cloud computing, the concept of vehicular clouds was introduced. Vehicular clouds rely on groups of vehicles whose corporate computing, sensing, communication, and physical resources can be coordinated and dynamically allocated to authorized users. Vehicular clouds differ from conventional cloud computing by employing untapped resources with distributed ownership. In a vehicular cloud, nodes are not available consistently due to random arrival and departure of vehicles. This creates a variable operating environment in which effectively assigning and completing assigned jobs becomes difficult. To address this challenge, we propose algorithms that incorporate redundancy. In this work, we provide a comparative resource utilization analysis by applying different algorithms with redundant and non-redundant implementations.

articleTitle: Decoding Justice: The Synergy of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in the Legal Landscape
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies holds significant promise for enhancing human-centric applications, particularly in the domain of law enforcement. This paper explores the application of AI and ML in crime prevention and resource allocation, pivotal areas of concern for law enforcement agencies (LEAs) globally. By utilizing historical crime data, sensory inputs, and advanced analytics, this study contributes to the evolving discourse on smart policing and proactive crime strategies. Our objective is to facilitate the transformation of LEAs from primarily reactive entities into proactive crime preventers through the adoption of predictive analytics, facial recognition enhanced surveillance, and natural language processing for efficient data analysis. We emphasize that collaborative efforts with AI experts ensure the responsible use of technology, meticulously balancing security imperatives with privacy concerns.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Control of a Bipedal Robot Using a Bond Graph Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The field of robotics is rapidly advancing, with particular focus on the study of bipedal locomotion, pushing the limits of what robots can achieve in terms of mobility and autonomy. Consequently, robotic locomotion has become a critical area of research in the development of bipedal robots. Various approaches exist for controlling bipedal gait cycles, utilizing different control techniques and advanced machine learning algorithms. Among these, artificial neural networks stand out as a highly effective supervised machine learning tool, used for prediction, classification, and control. In this paper, a successful gait cycle is defined by tracking the bipedal robot's center of gravity angle. An artificial neural network is employed as a controller to adapt the bond-graph model of the bipedal robot. This paper demonstrates the application of an artificial neural network as a machine learning algorithm to control and stabilize the locomotion of a bipedal robot with uniform response with overshot 0.25 for the linear velocity to overcome inertia and perform successful gait cycles.

articleTitle: Roads: Road Assistance for Driver Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The world is currently struggling with numerous tragic incidents on the roads and escalating difficulties in effectively managing road traffic. Li-Fi, or Light Fidelity, is a wireless communication technology that utilizes visible light, infrared, and ultraviolet spectrum to transmit data. V2V (Vehicle-to-Vehicle) communication refers to the exchange of data between vehicles using wireless communication technology. One of the technologies used to reduce such tragedies is the V2V which allows communication and the transfer of data between vehicles using wireless communications. In addition, with more technologies being introduced to the world of telecommunications, Li-Fi technology is gaining momentum in the wireless communication field using light as a transmission medium. The ROad Assistance for Driver Safety (ROADS) system integrates Li-Fi technology into V2V communication systems to enhance road safety and health monitoring; this was done by combining the use of LiFi technology with other technologies like obstacle detection to create a comprehensive and interconnected transportation network. The primary objective of ROADS is to close the existing gap in security in V2V communication by using LiFi technology. A heart rate sensor is also integrated into the steering wheel; alerts will be sent to paramedics or emergency contacts in case of emergencies. The findings and recommendations derived from this research will contribute to the ongoing efforts to create a safer and more efficient transportation ecosystem, with the potential to save lives.

articleTitle: WiFi Sensing for Presence Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Wi-Fi technology have enabled the development of smart infrastructure systems. Wi-Fi sensing refers to the noninvasive process of detecting human motion in indoor environments. This is achieved by exploiting the disturbances in the Wi-Fi signal caused by human motion. This technology enables a range of applications in security, healthcare monitoring and home automation, while offering a nonintrusive and cost-efficient solution. This paper focuses on device-free human presence detection using Channel State Information (CSI). The proposed framework leverages IoT devices to design a presence detection system using Deep Learning (DL) techniques including CNN and LSTM. Experimental results show that the proposed DL models tested in different environments achieved a robust generalization in both line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of sight (NLOS) scenarios, especially in through-the-wall scenario. On average, the proposed CNN model trained on periodogram of the CSI amplitude outperforms the other models and achieves an accuracy of 94%.

articleTitle: CampuScout: AIoT-Powered Guide for University Campus Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: Traditional guided tours in university settings are often resource-intensive, inflexible, and lack personalization, which can limit visitor engagement. This paper presents CampuScout, an AIoT-driven solution designed to provide autonomous and interactive university campus tours. Leveraging the advanced capabilities of the AIOT SerBot PrimeX, CampuScout integrates artificial intelligence (AI) with Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to offer real-time navigation, object detection, and dynamic interaction for both on-campus and remote visitors. The system utilizes AI for accurate object recognition and QR code interaction, creating an immersive educational experience that surpasses traditional human-guided tours in accessibility, efficiency, and user personalization. Real-world testing has demonstrated high detection accuracy rates and significant engagement improvements, providing a compelling alternative to conventional campus exploration. This paper also discusses system optimizations and outlines future enhancements to further improve the system's capabilities and user experience.

articleTitle: Novel Nakagami-$m$ Channel Model for G2A UAV Communications and Improved Security in Eavesdropping Dense Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: This work achieves improvement in secrecy capacity of values over 50 Mbit/s in the presence of a friendly airborne UAV where previously <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{s}$</tex> was less than 10Mbit/s. In addition to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{s}$</tex> estimation, a study on improving the outage probability of the network was also conducted showing that 10 times lower outages are achieved where previously 60% of the time the system was suffering from such outages. Finally, a closed-form solution is also presented for a Nakagami-m fading channel derived by the properties of a physical system based on the latest 3GPP standard, using a simulation setup for a dense urban environment using a 20MHz bandwidth signal with a center frequency of 2.4GHz with devices distanced from 50 to 650 m, aided by a UAV and in the presence of a UAV eavesdropper.

articleTitle: AeroNeuro-GlobalNet: Leveraging LEO Satellite Constellations and 5G/6G Networks for Real- Time Emotional Monitoring of Transport Operators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: In the pursuit of enhanced transport safety, the integration of advanced Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations with next-generation 5G and 6G networks presents a transformative solution for real-time monitoring of emotional states in high-risk transport operators, including truck drivers and airplane pilots. This study introduces AeroNeuro-GlobalNet, a pioneering approach that leverages deep learning architectures, specifically a multi-head attention based long short-term memory (MHA-LSTM) model, to process and analyze EEG signals for emotion detection. The system aims to identify critical emotional states that could compromise safety, such as stress or fatigue, thus providing a novel form of preventive safety measure in the transportation sector. Utilizing the ubiquitous coverage and high-speed capabilities of integrated LEO satellite and terrestrial networks, AeroNeuro-GlobalNet ensures consistent, global monitoring capabilities, crucial for applications where traditional communication systems falter, such as remote air routes and cross-country trucking paths. This paper outlines the development and implementation of the emotion detection system, addresses the challenges of real-time data processing and privacy concerns, and discusses the system's integration with existing transport communication infrastructures. By facilitating continuous monitoring and immediate response capabilities, AeroNeuro-GlobalNet aims to prevent potential accidents and enhance the overall safety of transport operations, reflecting a significant step forward in the application of AI and satellite technology in critical real-world applications. The proposed framework not only enhances transport safety but also sets a foundation for future research in the integration of biometric monitoring technologies with global network infrastructures, offering a scalable solution to a wide array of safety-critical applications in various sectors.

articleTitle: OLRAMT-DEC: Online Learning-Based Resource Allocation for AI Model Training in a Device-Edge-Cloud Continuum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The advancement of applications based on various Deep Neural Network (DNN) architectures, such as Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to an increasing need for the efficient utilization of network resources to meet the strict latency and computational requirements of model retraining. This paper proposes OLRAMT-DEC, an online learning-based device-edge-cloud cooperation framework to address the resource allocation problem for retraining AI models. We leverage the multi-armed bandit (MAB) framework to minimize the retraining latency, while considering time-varying channel conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in adapting to network dynamics through latency and regret minimization under different user loads. Furthermore, we show that our approach outperforms fixed and random allocation baselines in reducing latency toward the optimal benchmark in hindsight.

articleTitle: IoT-Enhanced Hybrid 5G-UAV Networks for Post-Catastrophe Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: In the aftermath of natural disasters, where ground communication infrastructures such as cell towers are often damaged, establishing wireless communication links for rescue teams becomes a formidable challenge. Effective communication is paramount in post-disaster response efforts, enhancing situational awareness and facilitating remote monitoring for collaboration among first responders. This underscores the critical role of 5G technology, with its promises of faster data transfer speeds, lower latency, and scalability to support numerous connected devices. Post-disaster challenges extend beyond infrastructure degradation, encompassing difficult access for rescue teams due to debris and potential exposure to toxic substances, hindering both communication and the collection of vital information on damage and victims. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) emerge as a pivotal solution, able to access hazardous areas. This paper advocates for the implementation of hybrid 5G-UAVs networks as a robust solution, combining the strengths of 5G with UAV capabilities to swiftly establish communication links in challenging post-disaster environments. Introducing three mobility models MA-GA, MC-PSO, MC-random for drone networks, we conduct a comparative analysis with classical algorithms. The study underscores the potential efficacy of hybrid 5G-UAVs networks in post-disaster scenarios, emphasizing technological innovation to address communication challenges in critical response efforts.

articleTitle: Next-Gen AIoT-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Health Management System for High-Speed Train Wheel and Axle Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: This paper proposes an AIoT-driven predictive maintenance and health management system specifically designed for high-speed train wheel and axle systems. By integrating advanced artificial intelligence techniques—such as Multi-Scale Transformer (MST) for accurate wheel wear prediction and Deep Wavelet Network (DWN) for precise axle stress analysis—within a comprehensive Internet of Things framework, the system enhances operational efficiency and safety. To address challenges like data quality, model interpretability, and real-time processing constraints, the research incorporates edge computing solutions to improve responsiveness. Experimental results demonstrate a 22% improvement in predictive accuracy for wheel wear and a 27.5% reduction in mean absolute error for stress prediction compared to traditional methods. Additionally, anomaly detection performance achieved an F1-score of 0.90, outperforming existing models by 26.8%. These findings validate the system's effectiveness and lay the groundwork for future advancements in intelligent railway systems, emphasizing data fusion, interpretable AI, and real-time processing capabilities.

articleTitle: A Novel Framework to Safeguard Inter-Vehicular Communication and Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: A novel framework is proposed to enhance security and privacy within Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs). Operating under a semi-honest threat model, the framework utilizes public-key cryptography for secure message exchange and dynamic key management, effectively mitigating security threats from compromised Roadside Units (RSUs) and malicious vehicles while preserving user privacy. Synchronized RSU communication maintains consistent security credentials across the network, enforcing uniform security standards. A partial trust model for RSUs, complemented by a blockchain-based fallback mechanism, strengthens RSU trustworthiness and integrity. An adaptive deregistration strategy efficiently removes vehicle credentials, reducing overhead in dense traffic scenarios, while dynamic key management sustains vehicle anonymity. To safeguard privacy, the framework employs pseudonymous public keys and encrypts both message content and metadata. Key performance metrics, including Message Delivery Ratio (MDR), Privacy Preservation Rate (PPR), and Security Breach Rate (SBR), were used to assess the system's efficacy. The framework achieved an MDR consistently high, demonstrating reliable message delivery even in high-traffic scenarios. It also recorded a high PPR, ensuring strong privacy protection, while maintaining a low SBR, reflecting superior resistance to security breaches. This comprehensive approach offers a robust solution for protecting inter-vehicular communication against specified threats and preserving privacy within VANETs.

articleTitle: DyStore: Dynamic Item Location Encoding and Navigation for Smart Locker Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: In logistics industry, hospitals and pharmacies, the demand for item storage management (e.g., item storage and access) is rapidly increasing and expanding. Intelligent item storage management systems based on Internet of Things (IoT) can largely save labor costs through contactless item dispensing and robotic item access. In this paper, we propose, DyStore, a framework of item location encoding and navigation that can encode the locations of cabinets, drawers, and boxes for efficient item access in an intelligent locker system. DyStore includes a user interface, a central control server, and an item storage system built upon cabinets/lockers. Given storage space constraints, we propose a hybrid data structure that combines trees and bitmaps for encoding the item locations. Additionally, DyStore employs a path planning algorithm to help access the stored items at the minimal time-distance combined cost. Results show that the performance of the data compression and path planning algorithms is superior to existing methods.

articleTitle: CAF-IoT: A Cybersecurity Assessment Framework for IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has become essential across various domains, including healthcare, industrial automation, critical infrastructure, and smart cities. However, its rapid evolution has introduced significant cybersecurity challenges, especially in hardware security and communication protocols. Successful cyberattacks can lead to catastrophic consequences, from data breaches to disruptions in critical infrastructure, highlighting the need for advanced cybersecurity measures and thorough cybersecurity assessments to guarantee the proper employment of these measures. Despite the growing concern, the literature still lacks comprehensive frameworks for evaluating the hardware security of IoT devices, with most studies primarily focusing on software vulnerabilities and other layers in the IoT system. This paper proposes a novel framework for assessing cybersecurity of IoT devices (CAF-IoT), tailored for hardware security including hardware components, communication protocols and buses within the perception layer. The framework automates vulnerability assessments, identifies security risks, and recommends mitigation strategies. The framework is validated through real-time penetration testing experimentation against several IoT devices, demonstrating its effectiveness in exploring various attack surfaces and detecting and analyzing existing vulnerabilities for enhanced security evaluation.

articleTitle: A Proposed Maintenance 4.0 Model for Laboratory Ventilation Systems: An Industry 4.0 Approach to Air Quality Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)

authors.preferredName: Hazza Muhsen Abdoul Qader Al Ameri

abstract: Air quality plays a crucial role in the health and well-being of workers, with poor conditions potentially leading to respiratory issues, headaches, fatigue, and decreased productivity. This study utilizes Industry 4.0 configuration to assess air quality in laboratory settings and develop an online maintenance planning model for ventilation systems, termed Maintenance 4.0. In a laboratory at UAE University, air quality monitoring devices were installed to measure parameters such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> emissions, humidity, PM1, PM2.5, PM10, and temperature. Several assessment procedures were employed to enhance the evaluation of ventilation system performance, referencing standards like ASHRAE 62.1, the World Health Organization (WHO) Air Quality Guidelines, and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) regulations. Additionally, predictive models were created using the collected data: one to forecast future air quality based on historical trends, and another-a Vector Autoregression (VAR) time series model-to predict air quality for the next 20 readings. The findings provide valuable insights into the current state of laboratory air quality and support the development of improvement strategies. By assessing ventilation performance and suggesting optimal maintenance times, this research benefits laboratory managers, maintenance personnel, and workers, enabling proactive measures through accurate air quality predictions and ultimately enhancing safety and productivity in laboratory environments.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Anomaly Detection Framework for Improving IoT System Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: Nowadays, Internet of Things (IoT) become progressively a fundamental part of our life. It revolutionizes various industries by enabling seamless connectivity between devices as well as it increases automation and efficiency. However, the reliability of IoT systems is often compromised due to the complexity and scale of these networks. It makes them vulnerable to failures and security breaches. To mitigate this problem, anomaly detection using artificial Intelligence (AI) in IoT can be a promising candidate to help data identifies unusual patterns that could indicate system faults or threats. In this paper, AI-Driven Anomaly Detection Framework for Enhancing IoT Security is proposed. The proposed framework enhances IoT system reliability by reducing downtime, improving security, and ensuring the consistent performance of connected devices. The experimental results demonstrate the efficiency of machine learning techniques and their capabilities with anomalies to enhance detection capability. Finally, the empirical results show that DT and RF outperform the other competitive models for network intrusion detection in the face of anomaly detection in front of the ongoing.

articleTitle: Optimizing Laboratory Safety Compliance Using Computer Vision: Real-Time PPE Detection in Laminar Flow Cabinets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: This research focuses on enhancing laboratory safety through an AI-powered Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) detection system using a customized YOLOv8 model. With current safety protocols requiring robust monitoring of PPE usage, the aim was to develop a scalable model for real-time compliance detection. Methodologically, a dataset of 2367 images was employed, trained, and validated on Roboflow servers, employing SGD with tailored parameters. Results indicate a 95% accuracy in PPE detection, with a 98.4% detection rate and 99.9% false alarm rate, showcasing high operational efficiency. Integrating survey data furthered insights into real-world PPE usage patterns, crucial for deployment. Future efforts will focus on refining model limitations, expanding applications to diverse laboratory scenarios, and integrating user behavior analysis to bolster safety protocols comprehensively.

articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Service Industries: Exploring Federal and State Regulations and Assessing Benefits and Concerns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: As service industries increasingly integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) initiatives, their significant impact on service operations and customer behavior is undeniable [1]. Nevertheless, it is crucial to recognize that prior literature may have been overly optimistic about AI implementation. There is a growing need to examine its potential benefits and concerns for consumers, businesses, and society at large [1].This research focuses on insurance companies as a business model and introduces three approaches to gain comprehensive insights into this evolving field, with a particular emphasis on the potential benefits that AI can bring to the industry. First, the study explores governmental policies and regulations related to AI in the insurance sector providing insights into the legal framework. Second, It delves into service interactions to understand how AI affects customer experiences in service delivery, analyzing 263 responses to gain insights into customer experience. Finally, the research explores risks associated with AI integration, including data privacy concerns and the potential for biased decision-making. By identifying key factors and research gaps within each category, the study aims to provide a holistic understanding of the potential adverse outcomes of AI-based services and offer valuable insights to scholars and practitioners ultimately fostering a more informed discourse on the integration of AI in service operations.

articleTitle: Drone-Based Data Collection for Precision Agriculture Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: Precision agriculture uses advanced technology to enhance farming methods and increase productivity. This study presents an innovative drone-based system integrated with a connected sensor network to autonomously collect data from lowpower, wireless underground sensor nodes that monitor essential soil parameters. The system utilizes a drone equipped with an Xbee communication module to gather and store data on an onboard SD card for further analysis. Field tests demonstrated stable flight performance and reliable data transmission over distances up to 100 meters, with the drone maintaining an average speed of 5 meters per second. Sensor nodes were strategically deployed to ensure complete data coverage across the agricultural field. Optimized flight trajectories allowed the drone to cover up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4 5 0 0}$</tex> meters in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15-m i n u t e$</tex> flight, which effectively monitors areas up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4 0, 0 0 0}$</tex> square meters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}$</tex> hectares) per flight. Power consumption analysis indicated that the drone operates at approximately 100 watts per flight, while sensor nodes consume 0.1 watts due to their energy-efficient sleep mode. The integration of IoT technology in this drone-based system highlights its effectiveness for precision agriculture. This approach provides an autonomous, cost-effective, and user-friendly solution for data collection that enhances agricultural monitoring and management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Mobility with Iot: A Versatile Parking Solution Integrating Real-Time Surveillance and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: This paper proposes and implements a versatile IoTenabled parking solution that provides real-time statistics on available parking spaces and includes a surveillance system to detect unusual vehicle behavior using a license plate recognition solution. Efficient algorithms are introduced to develop a parking perception system, utilizing advanced machine learning models such as YOLO-v5 and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for object detection and classification, providing precise parking lot statistics. Furthermore, the study presents an innovative approach to accurately identify vehicle number plates to monitor unusual behavior. A custom dataset was developed, and the proposed solutions were evaluated using various metrics.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Security Through Sentiment Analysis: A Framework for Improved Threat Detection and Adaptive Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: Due to the massive deployment of IoT devices, security has become an issue of significant concern because conventional approaches do not suit the growing and ever-changing variety of threats. The possibility to apply such a sentiment analysis in the context of security frameworks of IoT networks can be considered a valuable addition to the current approaches to threat detection and response. This research has sought to design and test a sentiment-based IoT security model to deal with increased detection of correct, minimal false alarms, and the ability to respond to users' feelings. We used the novel BERT and other transformations of the sentiment to measure their effectiveness in strengthening IoT security besides regular security measures. The evaluation of the framework's performance was done by using different criteria such as the detection rate, number of false positive results, and response time. The enhanced detection rate was observed up to 94.2% through BERT with minimizing the false positive up to 6. 2% through sentiment analysis integration. However, it was complemented with a moderate response time impact. This is an illustration of how sentiment analysis can be used to improve the security of IoT systems as shown through the proposed framework. Although it brings enhanced threat detection and non-customer-oriented responses, optimization of its threat detection and operational efficiency is apparent. Subsequent studies will continue refining the sentiment analysis models for real-time operation while expanding the array of emotional domains to enhance the solidness of the system.

articleTitle: Auction-Based Scheduling for Efficient Execution of Stochastic Tasks in Diverse Vehicular Clouds with Flexible Time Datacenter Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: In the realm of vehicular cloud computing, the Flexible Time Datacenter (FTDC) addresses the dynamic and unpredictable nature of vehicle availability and computational resource allocation. This paper presents the FTDC framework, which leverages a truthful reverse auction mechanism for efficient and strategic resource allocation between vehicles and tasks. The framework ensures that vehicles with computational resources are effectively matched with tasks based on their specific requirements. A key component of this framework is its robust task mitigation strategy, which addresses challenges arising from unexpected vehicle departures or task interruptions. This strategy involves dynamic task reallocation, where tasks are promptly reassigned to alternative vehicles or re-auctioned to ensure deadlines are met. The system incorporates penalties for premature departures and incentives for reliable behavior to maintain system integrity and efficiency. The FTDC framework is evaluated through a series of simulations that demonstrate its effectiveness in managing dynamic task allocation, resource utilization, and system reliability. The results highlight the framework's ability to adapt to unpredictable conditions while maintaining high performance and minimizing task delays.

articleTitle: DECML: Distributed Edge Consensus Machine Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The increasing reliance on interdependent datadriven services in the Internet of Things (IoT), smart homes, and Industry 4.0 is hindered by siloed security and privacy measures. Existing solutions like federated learning and distributed machine learning, with their various approaches such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, while promising, face challenges in ensuring robust security and privacy. We introduce Distributed Edge Consensus Machine Learning (DECML), a novel framework that enables secure, privacypreserving insights sharing among multiple stakeholders without exposing underlying data or models. DECML distributes queries and aggregates responses through independent nodes, achieving accuracy comparable to local deployments with minimal added latency. Our evaluation, using standard datasets and a 20-node network, demonstrates DECML's potential for collaborative decision-making without compromising privacy. This has significant implications for domains such as cybersecurity, healthcare, and financial services, where privacy concerns hinder data sharing.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Steganalysis Model for Color Images Using Statistical Texture Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Global Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (GCAIoT)
abstract: The increasing reliance on the internet and social media platforms has raised significant concerns about data security, especially in digital images. Typically, the combination of large data capacity, widespread use, complexity, and perceptual masking properties makes images a versatile and effective medium for hiding secret data through steganography. While steganography has legitimate uses such as secure communication and digital watermarking, it can be exploited for illegal activities. In this research work, we propose a steganalysis deep learning-based neural networks model to detect the presence of secret data in colored images using statistical features correlations and deep learning classification. To increase the automated detectability of the presence of hidden data in images, statistical texture features were extracted for each single channel of an image from a benchmark dataset of RGB color images by analyzing the spatial relationships between pairs of pixels in the image to generate a feature set using Gray Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM). This feature set is then fed into a deep learning steganalysis classification model using artificial neural networks (ANNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for hidden data detection. We used a validation approach and selected the best parameter values to enhance the performance of our deep learning steganalysis model. To evaluate the performance of the proposed models we used a public dataset of 10,000 uncompressed images using detection accuracy metrics. After conducting multiple experiments, the best result (Accuracy = 92.15%) was achieved using our CNN model.
